idea-plugin.name: Emberkai Icons
idea-plugin.description:
Emberkai Icons brings the Symbols file and folder icon set to JetBrains IDEs, as a companion to the Emberkai theme.

Java and Kotlin declarations keep their native IntelliJ type icons and badges.

Gradle Kotlin build scripts and version catalogs use Gradle icons. Spring Boot configuration and Helm charts have context-aware icons, and Spring XML configuration uses Emberkai artwork. Spring Modulith package locks are painted onto Emberkai folders when that plugin is installed.

Includes CI pipelines (including CircleCI, Tekton, and Bazel), Ansible, infrastructure as code (including Packer, Vagrant, and Nomad), database migrations, OpenAPI and AsyncAPI contracts, Avro schemas, Kubernetes, Kustomize, Flux, Argo CD, and Skaffold, Sealed Secrets, External Secrets, and SOPS, Quarkus, Micronaut, and Ktor configuration, JVM quality tooling, developer-tool configuration, and test assets.

Symbols-style project folders retain source/test colors, resource and package markers, and blue module/source-set badges, including Kotlin Multiplatform. Opt-in module-aware accents give every IntelliJ module a stable color that service roots, source roots, packages, and their descendants share. Opt-in JVM architecture folders give controller, service, repository, domain, and similar packages distinct icons.

Production, staging, test, and local variants of Spring profiles, Docker Compose files, Helm values, and .env files get shape-and-color environment badges, and so do environment folders such as overlays/production/, along with the configuration files inside them. Production files open with a red-tinted editor tab and a warning banner, each switched separately under Emberkai Icons | Editor Warnings. Private keys, keystores, .env files, and similar credentials that sit in a VCS root without being ignored get a red stop-sign warning badge, and so do Kubernetes manifests that hold a plaintext Secret. Spring profile files activated by the selected run configuration get a ring-and-dot live marker, and module folders with a live run or debug session get a running marker that names the configuration and Spring Boot port.

An amber warning badge marks problems that would otherwise surface late: Flyway migrations that share a version with a sibling, or that this branch added below the default branch's latest version; Liquibase changelogs that repeat a changeSet; a Helm Chart.lock that is out of date with Chart.yaml; workflows, Dockerfiles, and manifests with unpinned actions or latest images; and profile, Helm values, and .env variants that lack a key all their siblings define. Generated files get a grey generated hint, and those marked by their header are reported to the IDE as generated, so it warns before you edit them.

Spring, Quarkus, Micronaut, and JPA classes show a stereotype icon in place of the letter on the native Java/Kotlin class icon, under the IDE's own marks: applications, controllers, message listeners, scheduled jobs, HTTP clients, services, repositories, configuration classes, and entities. Test classes show whether they start containers, the whole application, or a Spring Boot test slice. Next.js routes and NestJS controllers, gateways, jobs, services, modules, and TypeORM entities get the same roles as a small badge on their TypeScript and JavaScript file icons.

Configure everything under Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Emberkai Icons with a live preview, including accessibility modes: a colorblind-friendly palette, high-contrast markers, monochrome folders, and reduced folder color. Quick toggles live in View | Emberkai Icons.

Each corner of an icon means one thing: top-left what a class does, top-right something to act on or live now, bottom-left the environment, bottom-right the artwork. View | Emberkai Icons | Icon Legend shows every mark with its meaning. Right-click a file or folder in the Project view, or an editor tab, and choose Explain This Icon to see what its marks mean and which rule or mapping selected it. Project view tooltips describe recognized tool files, project roles, environment variants, and module accents. Run Tools | Audit Project Icon Coverage to find files that still use generic icons.

Emberkai scopes such as Emberkai: Database migrations and Emberkai: Production config use the same recognition in Find in Files, the Project view, inspections, and File Colors.

Choose a lens under View | Emberkai Icons | Lens, such as Production blast radius, Infrastructure, or Entry points, to keep matching files in full color and dim the rest of the Project view. Changed on this branch highlights the files the current Git branch touches, including uncommitted ones. Hotspots highlights the files changed in the most commits over the last 90 days, adjustable under Emberkai Icons | Lenses, and Depends on highlights a module and every module that depends on it. A status bar widget shows the active lens and Spring profile and switches either with one click.

Repositories with a CODEOWNERS file show each file's owners in Project view tooltips and Explain This Icon, with an Emberkai: Owned by scope and lens for every owner. A No Owner lens and scope show files CODEOWNERS leaves unowned, and an inspection flags CODEOWNERS lines that match nothing. Tools | Find Reviewers for This Branch lists the owners of every file the current branch changes.

Icons by Miguel Solorio, from vscode-symbols.
